guard_patterns.handling: Require directly accessible official public source.
Keep provisional and final statistics distinct.
Preserve monthly, quarterly and annual reference periods and publication lags.
Keep activity, stock, generation and waste tonnage distinct from GHG emissions.
Keep point and fugitive industrial releases distinct.
Retain suppressed site-detail and coverage limitations.
Keep UK ETS installation, aviation and maritime scopes and effective dates explicit.
No parcel emission value without parcel geometry, identity, activity and method binding.
Every control must pass deterministic structure and scope checks.

packages.title: DESNZ Energy Trends provisional-status QA
facts: The 30 June 2026 Energy Trends and Prices release is an Accredited Official Statistics release.
The release describes its latest monthly energy statistics as provisional.
Production statistics are included.
Trade statistics are included.
Electricity-generation statistics are included.
Consumption statistics are included.
Statistics are supplied by fuel as well as total energy.
Coal, oil, gas and electricity are distinct fuel categories.
Provisional energy activity data must not be labelled final GHG inventory data.
National energy statistics do not constitute parcel emissions measurements.

packages.title: DESNZ Energy Trends fuel-separation QA
facts: Energy Trends separates major fuel families.
Electricity generation is distinct from electricity consumption.
Gas statistics are distinct from electricity statistics.
Oil statistics are distinct from coal statistics.
Fuel quantities are activity statistics rather than direct parcel GHG values.
Generation statistics can inform energy-system context.
Consumption statistics can inform activity context.
Fuel-specific statistics should not be merged without explicit conversion logic.
Conversion to GHG requires compatible factors and reference periods.
Parcel attribution requires a separate local binding step.

packages.title: DESNZ renewables capacity/generation publication-lag QA
facts: The UK renewables page was updated on 9 July 2026.
It reports renewable electricity capacity.
It reports renewable electricity generation.
It reports renewable electricity load factors.
It reports liquid biofuels consumption.
ET 6.1 and ET 6.2 are quarterly tables.
Quarterly ET 6.1 and ET 6.2 data are one quarter in arrears.
Publication lag must be preserved when comparing to same-day operational data.
Renewable capacity is not equivalent to avoided emissions.
National renewable statistics do not supply parcel-specific GHG values.

packages.title: DESNZ solar deployment monthly-lag QA
facts: DESNZ publishes solar photovoltaic deployment in ET 6.3.
ET 6.3 is a monthly table.
The table covers UK solar photovoltaic capacity deployment.
Monthly solar data are one month in arrears.
The page distinguishes monthly solar data from quarterly renewable tables.
ROCs data have a different publication schedule.
ROCs data are three months in arrears.
Capacity and certificate data are not direct emissions measurements.
Technology deployment cannot be converted to parcel GHG without local system data.
Version and reference month must be preserved.

packages.title: DfT Q1-2026 zero-emission vehicle stock QA
facts: DfT published Q1 2026 vehicle licensing statistics on 15 July 2026.
769,000 vehicles were registered for the first time in the UK in Q1 2026.
150,000 zero-emission vehicles were registered for the first time in Q1 2026.
First registrations increased 5.1% versus Q1 2025.
Zero-emission first registrations increased 12.9% versus Q1 2025.
There were 42.4 million licensed vehicles at end-March 2026.
There were 2.148 million licensed zero-emission vehicles at end-March 2026.
Licensed zero-emission vehicles increased 29.6% versus March 2025.
Vehicle stock statistics are not vehicle-use emissions measurements.
National vehicle stock cannot be assigned to a parcel without location and activity evidence.

packages.title: DfT zero-emission registration versus use-emissions QA
facts: Vehicle licensing statistics measure registrations and licensed stock.
A zero-emission registration category does not describe distance travelled.
Licensed stock does not describe road-link activity.
Registration counts do not provide electricity-consumption data.
Registration counts do not provide lifecycle emissions.
Registration counts do not provide parcel-level charging activity.
Road-transport emissions require activity and emission-factor methods.
Vehicle statistics can support fleet-composition context.
Fleet context must remain separate from measured emissions.
Parcel GHG remains null without parcel-specific activity evidence.

packages.title: Defra residual-waste treatment-scope QA
facts: Defra uses a treatment-based residual-waste definition in this release.
The measure includes waste originating in England sent to landfill in the UK.
It includes waste originating in England put through incineration in the UK.
It includes qualifying energy recovery.
It includes waste sent outside the UK for energy recovery.
Waste treated in England but originating elsewhere is excluded from the England-origin measure.
Major mineral wastes are excluded from the residual-waste-excluding-MMW measure.
Municipal residual waste has its own scope definition.
Waste tonnage is activity data and is not methane or CO2e by itself.
Parcel emissions require separate treatment-process and site-binding evidence.

packages.title: Defra residual-waste 2019 methodology-break QA
facts: The residual-waste publication identifies a time-series break in 2019.
Pre-2019 figures use a different methodology from 2019-2024 estimates.
Historic figures do not fully account for waste movements into and out of England.
Historic treatment accounting differs from the newer series.
Comparisons across the break must be made with care.
2019-2024 estimates support current residual-waste target monitoring.
Methodology version is part of the evidence provenance.
A trend crossing the methodology break must not be treated as fully like-for-like.
Waste trend statistics do not directly quantify GHG emissions.
Parcel attribution is a separate downstream step.

packages.title: Defra municipal landfill/incineration shift QA
facts: Municipal residual waste sent to landfill was 7.6 million tonnes in 2024.
Municipal residual waste put through incineration including Energy from Waste was 16.8 million tonnes in 2024.
Municipal residual waste sent outside the UK for energy recovery was 1.7 million tonnes in 2024.
Landfill tonnage decreased 23.3% between 2019 and 2024.
Incineration tonnage increased 23.1% between 2019 and 2024.
Per-person landfill residual waste fell to 130 kg in 2024.
Per-person incineration residual waste was 286 kg in 2024.
Treatment-route shifts can affect emissions profiles but do not directly quantify GHG.
Energy-from-Waste tonnage is not equivalent to electricity generated or CO2e emitted.
Site-level emissions need plant-specific reporting or modelling.

packages.title: Environment Agency Waste Data Interrogator site-coverage QA
facts: The 2024 Waste Data Interrogator record was updated 5 June 2026.
It includes waste received at permitted sites.
It includes waste removed from permitted sites.
It provides summary tables for England and former planning regions.
Regulated waste-management operators report quantities and waste types.
The dataset is calendar-year based.
It covers around 6,000 regulated sites.
The data support compliance monitoring and planning.
Waste quantity records do not by themselves provide greenhouse-gas emissions.
Parcel use requires matching a permitted facility to the relevant parcel geometry.

packages.title: Environment Agency WDI confidentiality/site-detail guard QA
facts: Operator waste returns are generally public-register information.
Commercial-confidentiality claims can suppress site details.
Confidential records can remain in aggregated figures without site attribution.
The dataset does not include details of waste producers.
Facility identity and waste-producer identity are different concepts.
Missing site detail must not be guessed from aggregated totals.
Aggregated tonnage must not be attributed to a specific parcel.
Confidentiality status is a provenance constraint.
Site coverage does not imply all waste origins are known.
Parcel binding requires an independently verified site identity and geometry.

packages.title: Environment Agency Pollution Inventory point/fugitive-source QA
facts: The Pollution Inventory includes annual mass releases of specified substances.
It covers releases to air.
It covers releases to controlled waters and sewers.
It also records quantities of waste transferred off site.
The inventory covers large industrial sites regulated by the Environment Agency.
Reporting covers the whole authorisation or permit.
Reporting can include non-point and fugitive releases such as leaks.
Reporting can also include specific point sources such as chimneys.
Point and fugitive releases must remain distinguishable where the data support that distinction.
Permit-level emissions are not automatically parcel-bound emissions.

packages.title: Environment Agency Pollution Inventory permit-boundary QA
facts: Pollution Inventory reporting is tied to an authorisation or permit boundary.
Large industrial authorisations require annual reporting of reportable substances.
A permit can encompass multiple release points.
A permit can include fugitive emissions.
A permit-level total can therefore be broader than a single stack.
The 2024 dataset was added on 17 April 2026.
Historical downloadable files cover 2013-2024 on the current record.
Permit scope must be preserved during source matching.
A point location must not be treated as the full spatial footprint of all permit emissions.
Parcel attribution needs explicit permit-to-parcel geometry evidence.

packages.title: UK ETS Registry compliance-report boundary QA
facts: The UK ETS reports collection was published in January 2026.
The collection links public reports from the UK ETS Registry.
Registry reports include annual compliance reporting on emissions.
Registry reports include surrendered allowances.
Registry reports include account-holder lists.
Installation, aircraft-operator and trader account types are distinct.
Allowance allocation and verified emissions are different measures.
Surrendered allowances are compliance instruments rather than physical emissions measurements by themselves.
Registry reporting can support operator-level verification.
Parcel attribution remains a separate geometry and installation-identity gate.

packages.title: UK ETS verified-reporting and surrender-date QA
facts: UK ETS operators within scope have annual monitoring and reporting duties.
Covered businesses must provide independently verified emissions reports.
The standard annual reporting deadline is 31 March following the reporting year for relevant sectors.
Allowances are surrendered against reportable emissions under the scheme rules.
Allowance surrender and emissions reporting are related but not identical records.
Deficit processes can apply where sufficient allowances are not surrendered.
Compliance records should preserve the scheme year.
Verified emissions are installation or operator records, not parcel measurements.
Scheme scope should be checked before using a record as an emissions candidate.
Parcel binding requires installation identity plus parcel geometry.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime July-2026 scope-version QA
facts: The Participating in the UK ETS guidance was updated on 1 July 2026.
The UK ETS scope has expanded to domestic maritime activity from July 2026.
Maritime operators have a dedicated monitoring and reporting framework.
Maritime scheme-year obligations differ from legacy UK MRV arrangements.
The previous UK MRV regime was superseded as the ETS maritime system came into effect.
Effective dates must be preserved when using maritime emissions evidence.
Pre-expansion and post-expansion records should not be silently merged.
Maritime operator records are not land-parcel emissions records.
Port calls do not automatically assign ship emissions to a port parcel.
Parcel-level use requires a separate allocation methodology.

packages.title: UK ETS installation-scope versus parcel QA
facts: UK ETS covers regulated installations in energy-intensive industries and power generation.
It also covers aviation and, from July 2026, domestic maritime scope under applicable rules.
Installation coverage follows scheme definitions rather than cadastral parcel boundaries.
A regulated installation can span multiple physical assets.
A parcel can contain assets that are outside an installation reporting boundary.
An installation emissions record is therefore not automatically a parcel total.
Operator and installation identifiers should be preserved.
Scheme status should be preserved by year.
Verified emissions can strengthen an industrial source candidate.
Parcel GHG remains unbound until installation geometry is matched to parcel geometry.

packages.title: Energy-mix to parcel-emissions non-inference QA
facts: Energy Trends provides national production and consumption statistics.
Renewables tables provide national capacity and generation statistics.
Electricity tables provide generation, supply, consumption and fuel-use statistics.
These sources can describe grid and energy-system context.
National generation mix is not a meter-level consumption record.
Meter consumption is not a parcel emission measurement unless the meter is bound to the parcel.
Grid factors require a compatible reference period and method.
On-site generation can alter local electricity accounting.
Operational and embodied emissions are different concepts.
No parcel value is produced from national energy mix alone.

packages.title: Waste-activity to GHG non-inference QA
facts: Waste Data Interrogator reports waste quantities and movements.
Residual-waste statistics classify treatment routes.
Landfill methane research measures residual methane using dedicated methods.
Pollution Inventory can report releases from regulated industrial permits.
Waste tonnage and methane emissions are not the same quantity.
Incineration tonnage and CO2 emissions are not the same quantity.
Treatment technology and waste composition affect emissions.
Site-specific emissions require site reporting or a validated emissions model.
Waste-origin geography and treatment-site geography can differ.
Parcel GHG is not inferred from waste tonnage alone.

packages.title: Cross-source version/time-base composite guard QA
facts: Energy Trends June 2026 contains provisional monthly statistics.
Renewables quarterly tables are published one quarter in arrears.
Solar deployment monthly tables are one month in arrears.
DfT Q1 2026 vehicle statistics use a January-March reference period.
Waste Data Interrogator 2024 uses calendar-year data.
Residual-waste estimates have a methodology break around 2019.
Pollution Inventory 2024 is annual permit-level reporting.
UK ETS compliance records are scheme-year records.
Cross-source comparisons must align reference period, geography, scope and measurement type.
No cross-source composite may be labelled parcel emissions until parcel-binding evidence is verified.
